record.paper_title: Two open problems in graph theory
record.original_question: Let a finite simple graph G with at least four edges be represented by the collection of all edge-deleted subgraphs obtained by removing each edge of G once. Is G uniquely reconstructible from that collection?

evidence.quote: One direction that ought to prove fruitful, though it has not yet come to fruition, is edge reconstruction. Instead of removing the vertices one at a time from a graph, remove edges.

Like the vertex-deleted case, there are some small graphs which do not satisfy the obvious edge-deleted reconstruction conjecture. So we have to restrict our attention to graphs with at least 4 edges.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite simple graph with at least four edges, and let E(G) = {e_1, ..., e_m} denote its edge set. Define the edge-deck of G to be the multiset

  D_e(G) = { G - e_i : i = 1, ..., m },

where each G - e_i is the subgraph obtained from G by deleting the edge e_i (keeping all vertices), and graphs in the multiset are considered up to isomorphism.

Say that G is edge-reconstructible if every finite simple graph H satisfying D_e(H) = D_e(G) (as multisets of isomorphism classes) is isomorphic to G.

Question: Is every finite simple graph G with at least four edges edge-reconstructible?
artifact.status_search_result: The Edge Reconstruction Conjecture, posed by Harary in 1964, remains open in general. Substantial partial results are known (e.g., Lovász/Müller-type sufficient conditions in terms of edge counts, and Hemminger's reduction relating edge reconstruction to vertex reconstruction of line graphs), but no proof or counterexample is known for all graphs with at least four edges.

status_evidence.title: Reconstruction conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The edge reconstruction conjecture of Harary (1964) states that graphs with at least four edges are determined by their edge-decks; it remains an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The edge reconstruction conjecture is still an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Graph Reconstruction and Structure (Jane Tan, Oxford)
status_evidence.snippet: The Edge Reconstruction Conjecture is also wide open... a result of Hemminger says that a graph (apart from K3) is edge-reconstructible iff its line graph is reconstructible.
status_evidence.claim: Recent thesis confirms the edge reconstruction conjecture remains open.
